title: Mixed not-all-equal knots on the weave: one broken bond per knot, matchings, and when they stay bipartite
claim: In a weave of not-all-equal-class knots each knot has exactly one bond broken in its own signs; allowed states up to the global flip are perfect matchings of the honeycomb with every inconsistent bond subdivided (trivial torus sector); per cell 2 = 2u + i, so more than two inconsistent bonds per cell empties the base and period-one arrangements have i = 0 or 2; the matching graph is bipartite iff every distinction meets an even number of inconsistent bonds.
standard_statement: Frustrated Ising triangles with one unsatisfied bond; Moessner-Sondhi Ising-dimer mapping with subdivided edges; planar bipartiteness by face parity.
prior_work: Wannier 1950; Blote and Hilhorst 1982; Moessner and Sondhi 2001; Kasteleyn; Kenyon, Okounkov and Sheffield 2006; Fendley, Moessner and Sondhi 2002; WEAVE-LAWS-20261117-001A.
completion_gate: check.py passes (brute force on 4 x 4 weaves), the referee reviews the proofs.
